projects.title: The STEM Room
projects.hook: Thirteen workshops. One bench.
projects.description: The collection's science bench under one roof: Everyday Physics, Everyday Sound, Everyday Time, Everyday Light, Everyday Chemistry, Everyday Electronics, Everyday Measure, Everyday Engineering, Everyday Math, Everyday Earth, Everyday Computing, Everyday Body, and The Radio Room — thirteen full workshops gathered behind one door, each keeping its own page, its own benches, and its own address.
projects.starter: Play a pool shot in Everyday Physics, or press the Groove Salad preset in The Radio Room.
projects.detail: Landing room · 13 workshops under one roof: physics · sound · time · light · chemistry · electronics · measure · engineering · math · earth · computing · body · radio

projects.title: Everyday Physics
projects.hook: Play the shot. See the physics.
projects.description: Shoot pool on a table that draws the reflection angles and hands the momentum over in front of you, launch projectiles on a 60-metre range where gravity bends every flight into the same curve, time a pendulum that only cares about its string, balance a seesaw on one multiplication — and try four experiments at the kitchen table.
projects.starter: Aim the cue ball off a cushion and watch the two angles come out equal.
projects.detail: Playable pool table with physics overlays · ballistics launcher · pendulum & seesaw benches · 4 experiments · 8 verified links out

projects.title: Everyday Sound
projects.hook: The physics you can hear — and the mathematics it sings.
projects.description: Slide a tone from rumble to whistle and read its wavelength, weigh loudness honestly in decibels with the hearing-safety line attached, time echoes off walls and thunder off the sky, learn why a string sings and a drum thuds — then cross into music as mathematics: intervals as ratios with temperament's compromise shown in cents, rhythm as fractions that must sum to one, the circle of fifths as geometry, and a two-octave piano, synthesized live, that loads MIDI files, lights its keys as they play, and records your own playing into a real .mid you can keep.
projects.starter: Play the Ode to Joy demo on the little piano, then try to fill a 4/4 measure exactly.
projects.detail: Tone & decibel benches · string bench · echo & thunder ranging · intervals as ratios · two-octave piano with MIDI in & out · rhythm fractions · circle of fifths

projects.title: Everyday Time
projects.hook: The one measurement nobody can see — carved, corrected, and agreed.
projects.description: Draw a real horizontal sundial for your latitude and add up exactly why it disagrees with your clock (the equation of time, plus four minutes per degree of longitude — 37 minutes of it in Defiance alone), run any year through the leap-year machine's three gates and read the calendar's own drift beside the verdict, read one UTC moment on seven walls around the world with daylight saving confessed city by city, climb from a heartbeat to the age of the Earth and count the heartbeats in a lifetime, swing a pendulum at the speed its length dictates, and count days and weekdays between any two dates with the Julian centuries honestly flagged.
projects.starter: Set the sundial to 3 PM in Defiance and watch the shadow fall 33 degrees east of noon — then ask it why your clock disagrees.
projects.detail: Sundial bench with equation-of-time & longitude readout · leap-year machine · time zones bench · scale ladder & lifetime heartbeats · pendulum bench · days-between-dates

projects.title: Everyday Light
projects.hook: The fastest thing there is — slowed down, split, and mixed two ways.
projects.description: Split sunlight the way a prism does and mix colour the two opposite ways — lamps adding toward white, pigments subtracting toward a near-black that leaks (which is why printers carry black) — then strike colour chords on a twelve-hue wheel (complements straight across at 180°, triads at 120° steps: the circle of fifths' twin), bend light through a thin lens and watch the image land upside down, read the blue sky and the red sunset off the single 1/λ⁴ scattering rule, walk a stick's shadow around a compass through the day, and slide the spectrum past the ends of sight into infrared and ultraviolet, which are labelled, never painted.
projects.starter: Turn all three lamps up and make white — then mix all three paints at full and watch white disappear into a warm near-black.
projects.detail: Additive & subtractive mixing benches · colour-chord wheel (12 hues, chords by angle) · thin-lens ray bench · Rayleigh sky & sunset bench · shadows-through-the-day bench · spectrum slider 380–750 nm with IR/UV cards

projects.title: Everyday Chemistry
projects.hook: Everything is atoms. Atoms are countable.
projects.description: See any of 30 elements drawn as an atom, count neutrons step by step, type a formula and watch it counted and weighed, take familiar substances apart, and try eight kitchen experiments that each show a real idea about atoms and molecules.
projects.starter: Pick oxygen on the atom bench, then weigh C6H12O6 on the formula bench.
projects.detail: Visual atom bench · 30 elements · formula counter & molar-mass bench · 8 kitchen experiments · 5 verified links out

projects.title: Everyday Electronics
projects.hook: One small law runs every circuit.
projects.description: Run a live circuit and watch Ohm's law happen, solve for any voltage, current, or resistance with the working shown, find the resistor that keeps an LED alive, learn how a crystal radio works with no battery at all — and build one, plus a fruit battery, a paper circuit, and a throwie.
projects.starter: Close the switch on the circuit bench, then read how the crystal radio hears without a battery.
projects.detail: Live circuit bench · Ohm's law & LED resistor benches · crystal radio explained & built · fruit battery · 6 verified links out

projects.title: Everyday Body
projects.hook: Your body is a universe you carry around.
projects.description: Explore the Human Body Lab: preserve the organ atlas and twelve brain topics, locate 25 body regions from the front or back, connect muscles, bones, and nerves, then investigate five everyday observations in Body Detective.
projects.starter: Choose an upper arm in the body imager, explore its muscles, then investigate why the arm changes shape.
projects.detail: Human Body Lab · 25 body regions · muscles, bones & nerves · 5 Body Detective cases · 12 organs · 12 brain topics · scenarios & quiz

projects.title: Everyday Measure
projects.hook: One staircase of tens — and every measurement in the world is standing on it.
projects.description: The metric system for Americans: climb the prefix ladder (kilo means a thousand of them), convert length, weight, volume, and temperature with the working shown, feel the sizes against a nickel, a paperclip, and a 2-litre bottle, weigh an elephant in both systems at once, dodge the tonne/ton and gallon traps, and read how a unit mix-up cost a Mars orbiter and nearly cost an airliner.
projects.starter: Climb the ladder: start at kilo, land on centi, and watch 2.5 kilometres become 250,000 centimetres.
projects.detail: Interactive prefix ladder · 4 converter benches with working shown · feel-it anchors · comparison shelf · trap cards · breakage stories · short history

projects.title: Everyday Engineering
projects.hook: Six machines. One rule: force is multiplied, energy never is.
projects.description: The six simple machines with their disguises off — the lever in the bottle opener, the wheel & axle in the doorknob, the pulley in the flag pole, the ramp in the hill path, the wedge in the axe, and the screw as a ramp wrapped around a pole — with four benches that show their working: slide a fulcrum and lift a 90 kg crate, rig one to four pulley segments and pay in rope, push a load up a slope read against the 1:12 wheelchair-ramp standard, and shove a square frame to watch it rack while a triangle holds — plus the engineer's pocket log table: ninety mantissas, characteristic-plus-mantissa lookups, and interpolation the way three centuries of engineers computed. Cross-linked with The Survival Guide both ways: its field skills are these machines outdoors.
projects.starter: Slide the lever bench's fulcrum toward the crate and watch the 90 kg load lift with 18 kg of push — then look up log 500 in the pocket table.
projects.detail: Six simple machines · 5 benches with working shown: lever · pulley · ramp · frames · pocket log₁₀ table with interpolation · wedge & screw cards · the honest rules · field links to The Survival Guide

projects.title: Everyday Math
projects.hook: Every trick is a pattern. Every pattern has a reason.
projects.description: The numbers themselves — the tricks with their reasons showing (the nines table built from two columns, 0 to 9 down and 9 to 0 up; ×11 split-and-add; squares that end in 5), the checkers that catch bad arithmetic (divisibility rules, casting out nines — and its honest limit), the fractions and percents people freeze on, the formula shelf with worked examples, huge and tiny numbers in scientific notation with Avogadro's number bridging to Chemistry, the full log table with proportional parts, a printable sheet carrying the 16×16 times grid and the logs to 1000, and a scientific calculator that admits its last digit lies.
projects.starter: Write 0 to 9 down one column and 9 to 0 up the other, and read the whole nines table across — then check why every answer's digits add to 9.
projects.detail: The numbers themselves · tricks with reasons: the nines' two columns · ×11 · squares ending in 5 · divisibility · casting out nines · fractions & percents benches · formula shelf with worked examples · scientific notation & Avogadro's number · the full log table with proportional parts · printable 16×16 times grid & log sheet · a scientific calculator that admits its last digit lies

projects.title: Everyday Earth
projects.hook: The ground under your feet has a story in every layer.
projects.description: The planet from the ground down and the weather up: the water cycle as a working loop — evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection — with the honest line that your glass of water is older than the dinosaurs; the three rock families with the rocks you actually meet (granite countertops, limestone, marble) and the cycle that turns each into the others; soil in its horizons, topsoil first, with the centuries an inch of it costs; the Earth's layers at their true depths, measured against the deepest hole anyone has ever dug; and weather read from the ground — fronts, clouds, and a falling barometer — with doors to Wikipedia, the USGS, NOAA, Tonight's Sky, and the pocket Weather Everywhere.
projects.starter: Tap Evaporation on the water cycle and follow one glass of water all the way around — then ask the depth bench how far the deepest mine gets toward the core.
projects.detail: The planet, layer by layer · the water cycle bench · the rock sorter: 9 rocks, 3 families · the soil horizons · the depth bench: crust to core at true scale · weather from the ground: fronts · cloud spotter · barometer bench · 15 verified links out, incl. Tonight's Sky, Weather Everywhere, NOAA, USGS, and UC Davis's Earth Day

projects.title: Everyday Computing
projects.hook: On or off. Everything else is wiring.
projects.description: How a computer is built out of almost nothing: counting in twos on eight switches; the six gates that decide — AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, NOT — with truth tables that fill in as you play; two gates wired into a half adder, XOR for the sum and AND for the carry; a three-gate toy net that recognises one pattern in eight and counts its near misses; a free-form logic builder where you wire gates into circuits of your own, including an XOR assembled from the basic gates; the bit-to-terabyte ladder with the honest 1000-versus-1024 split; and algorithms as recipes a machine can follow exactly — with the gates-pattern infographic from Steven's aphorism posts on the wall, errors named, and a door back to the Nerd Heaven panel it came from.
projects.starter: Flip the eight switches to make 42 — then open the logic builder and load the XOR trick.
projects.detail: Counting in twos: the binary bench, 8 switches, 0–255 · the gates bench: AND · OR · XOR · NAND · NOR · NOT with live truth tables · gates that add: the half adder · the toy net: a 3-gate pattern recogniser · the logic builder: wire your own circuits · bits & sizes: the 1000 vs 1024 ladders · a program is a recipe: the sorting bench · the gates infographic, published as-is, errors named · 7 verified links out
